collection_log.query_or_url: TinaforOregon.com (referenced in pamphlet statement text; not fetched)

collection_notes: Steps 1-5 were run identically for every candidate in the US Senate, US House 1-6 and Governor races (the shared WebSearch budget ran out once mid-run and the remaining searches were completed after it reset). To keep effort equal, no T3 items are included for any candidate in these races: every item comes from the T1 voters' pamphlet, official .gov pages or official roll-call pages; promising T3 results are named in these notes for possible later, race-wide use. Campaign websites are recorded from the pamphlet but were not fetched for positions, for any candidate. oregonlive.com and apnews.com are rejected by the search proxy as allowed_domains, so step 5 used three fixed domain groups for everyone: (opb, oregoncapitalchronicle, wweek, ballotpedia), (kgw, koin, kptv, katu), (portlandmercury, vote411, pamplinmedia, portlandtribune). The Multnomah military/overseas online voters' guide was checked and contains no federal or governor statements. Pamphlet excerpts were obtained through a summarizing fetch limited to ~125-character quotes, so excerpts are short. Incumbency: Oregon Blue Book (T1) and pamphlet occupation 'Governor'. The oregon.gov 'Meet the Governor' page uses older campaign-era wording ('As Governor, Tina will be...') and was not used for positions. Pamphlet lists Democrat, Working Families; matches inventory. Website appears only in the statement's endorsement text, per the pamphlet extract. Step 5 surfaced substantial 2026 general-election T3 coverage for all three candidates (e.g. OPB 2026-07-23 'Could a third-party candidate shake up the Oregon governor's race?' on Smith; Portland Tribune 2026-08-26 on Drazan's proposals; OPB/KOIN on Kotek); not fetched, to keep T3 treatment identical across all assigned races. Much of the remaining coverage is polling/horse-race and excluded by policy.
